request.system:
You classify one recorded call at Aegis Cloud Security, a B2B SaaS company, against a fixed theme taxonomy (version v1).

You receive the full transcript as numbered turns in the form "[index] Speaker (side): sentence". side is "customer" (works at an outside company) or "aegis_staff" (works at Aegis). You are given nothing else about the call: no title, no call type, no summary. Judge only from the words in the transcript.

THEMES (what kind of conversation it is; pick by what the call is mostly about):
1. Commercial Renewals and Retention: Renewals, contracts, pricing and SLA negotiation, churn risk, expansion deals. Boundary: If a call is mainly about product adoption with renewal as an aside, use Product Adoption, Feedback and Expansion.
2. Product Adoption, Feedback and Expansion: Previews, launches, early access, roadmap input, feature requests, adoption and compliance-readiness reviews of the product, and internal launch-readiness reviews. Boundary: The module belongs in the product area field, not in the theme. Renewal talk that is only an aside stays here.
3. Incident and Outage Response: War rooms, root cause, remediation plans, customer impact assessment, incident communication, postmortems, reliability reviews. Boundary: A single customer's technical fault that is not a platform incident belongs in Technical Integration and Performance Issues.
4. Technical Integration and Performance Issues: Support-style troubleshooting: SSO, SAML, SCIM, LDAP, MFA failures, connectors and SIEM integration, backup windows and throughput, report defects, API errors, internal scalability concerns. Boundary: Module-specific problems go here with the module in the product area field. A platform-wide outage is Incident and Outage Response.
5. Onboarding and Implementation Scoping: Kickoffs, deployment planning, architecture scoping, setup workshops. Boundary: Troubleshooting of an already deployed integration is Technical Integration and Performance Issues.
6. Billing and Usage Disputes: Invoices, overages, seat counts, billing adjustments. Boundary: Small theme (about 4 calls in the pilot); kept because it is distinct and actionable.
7. Competitive Strategy and Win/Loss: Competitive intelligence, battlecards, win/loss analysis, and customer-facing calls where the customer is evaluating alternatives. Boundary: Definition widened from the pilot's internal-only version to include customer calls about evaluating alternatives.
8. Internal Planning and Delivery Cadence: Standups, sprint planning, retros, all-hands, design and roadmap syncs with no customer or incident focus. Boundary: If a meeting is mainly an incident, use Incident and Outage Response.

Other / new theme: use only if no theme above fits. Then describe the call in one sentence in other_description. Other / new theme only if no theme fits. More than 10% of calls in Other triggers a taxonomy revision (new version, full re-run).

PRODUCT AREA (which module the call is about; exactly one):
- Detect: Threat detection, event ingestion, alerting.
- Comply: Compliance reporting and evidence mapping (including Comply v2).
- Protect: Backup, snapshots, disaster recovery (includes backup).
- Identity: Directory sync, SSO, SAML, SCIM, MFA, IAM governance.
- Platform/General: No single product dominates, or the call is cross-product.

INCIDENT: Set incident to '2026-03-detect-outage' (otherwise null) when the call's main purpose, or a major part of it, is the March 2026 Detect event-processing pipeline outage: cause, impact, remediation, customer communication or aftermath. A separate field so the outage story is visible across support, external and internal calls.

Return one record with:
- primary_theme: exactly one theme name copied from the list above, or "Other / new theme".
- tags: zero, one or two further theme names from the list that also clearly come up. Never repeat the primary theme. Empty when primary_theme is "Other / new theme".
- product_area: exactly one product area name copied from the list.
- incident: "2026-03-detect-outage" or null.
- other_description: one sentence if primary_theme is "Other / new theme", otherwise an empty string.
- evidence_quote: a short passage of at most 30 words that best supports primary_theme, copied EXACTLY, character for character, from the sentence part of ONE turn. Copy only the words after "Speaker (side): ". Never include the index, the speaker name, the side or the colon prefix. Do not paraphrase, do not shorten with "...", do not join text from different turns.
- confidence: "high" if clearly about the primary theme, "medium" if two themes compete, "low" if it fits poorly.
- taxonomy_version: "v1".

Return only JSON matching the schema.

[5] Kendra Wallace (customer): It's pretty much every night. I mean, maybe slightly worse on weekends but honestly it's bad across the board. [6] David Kim (aegis_staff): Right, yeah, that makes total sense and that's a real operational concern. Um, let me ask — what's the approximate data volume you're backing up each night? Do you have a rough figure?
[7] Kendra Wallace (customer): It's around, uh, two to two and a half terabytes per night. That hasn't changed dramatically. I mean, we've grown a little but nothing that should cause this kind of slowdown.
[8] David Kim (aegis_staff): Got it. And have you made any changes on your end around that time — network configuration, storage infrastructure, anything like that? Or was this kind of just one day it started being slow?
[9] Kendra Wallace (customer): Not that I'm aware of. I mean, I had my team look into it and we didn't push any major infrastructure changes around that time. So we're kind of pointing the finger at your platform, honestly.
[10] David Kim (aegis_staff): I hear you, and I'm not here to deflect blame — I want to find the root cause wherever it is. Let me pull up your account and look at the job logs from the last couple weeks here.
[11] Kendra Wallace (customer): Please do. And while you're at it, I want to flag — we're running incremental backups, not full backups, so the fact that it's taking this long is extra concerning to me.
[12] David Kim (aegis_staff): Yeah, that's a really good point, incremental jobs should absolutely not be taking that long. Okay, I'm in your account now... I can see the job history here. Hmm. Okay so I'm seeing some things.
[13] Kendra Wallace (customer): What are you seeing? Because my team has been asking me for answers and I don't have any.
[14] David Kim (aegis_staff): So I can see that your backup jobs are completing, but the throughput rate has dropped significantly. You're running at roughly 120 to 140 megabytes per second, whereas historically your jobs were running closer to 400 or 500. That's the bottleneck.
[15] Kendra Wallace (customer): Okay so something changed on your end then. Because we didn't touch anything.
[16] David Kim (aegis_staff): It could be a few things — I want to dig into this more before I point fingers anywhere. One thing I'm noticing is that your backup agent version — you're running 3.4.1, and we released 3.6.0 back in late January. There were some performance optimizations in that release, specifically around incremental change detection.
[17] Kendra Wallace (customer): Wait — so you're saying there might be a performance issue in the version we're running and there's already a fix out?
[18] David Kim (aegis_staff): I don't want to say definitively that's the cause yet, but it is worth flagging. There was a known issue in 3.4.x where under certain conditions the change block tracking mechanism could — um — essentially over-scan, meaning it's processing more data than it needs to.
[19] Kendra Wallace (customer): David, that sounds like exactly what's happening. Why weren't we notified about this? This feels like something we should have gotten an email about or... I don't know, something.
[20] David Kim (aegis_staff): That's fair feedback and I'm going to note that in the case. Customers on affected versions should have been flagged for that update and I'll look into why that didn't happen for your account. That's a process gap we need to close.
[21] Kendra Wallace (customer): Yeah, I mean — look, I like Aegis, we've been customers for over a year and overall we've been happy. But this kind of thing is frustrating. We're a retail business, our data pipeline is critical, and three weeks of bad backups is not something I can just shrug off.
[22] David Kim (aegis_staff): Absolutely, and I'm not asking you to shrug it off. Let's focus on getting you fixed first and then I'll make sure the right people on our side hear this feedback. So — upgrading to 3.6.0, that's the immediate step I'd recommend. Can your team do that tonight?
[23] Kendra Wallace (customer): We can probably do it tonight or tomorrow night. What's involved in the upgrade? Is there any downtime, any risk?
[24] David Kim (aegis_staff): It's a rolling upgrade, so there's minimal impact. The agent restarts but the restart window is typically under two minutes. You'd want to do it outside your backup window obviously, but it shouldn't cause any data issues or anything like that.
[25] Kendra Wallace (customer): Okay. And what if we do the upgrade and it's still slow? Then what?
[26] David Kim (aegis_staff): If you're still seeing the issue after the upgrade, the next thing I'd want to look at is your network egress path — specifically whether there's any throttling or rate limiting happening between your environment and our ingestion endpoints. I can also set you up with enhanced logging on the next backup run so we get more granular telemetry.
[27] Kendra Wallace (customer): Okay, that's fine. I mean I'm hopeful the upgrade fixes it but I've been hopeful before with this and it hasn't gotten better on its own.
[28] David Kim (aegis_staff): I get it. I don't want to just give you hope and disappear — here's what I'll do. I'm going to send you the upgrade instructions in writing right after this call, and I'll personally follow up with you on Monday morning to check on how the backup ran. I'll keep this case open until we confirm the performance is back to where it should be.
[29] Kendra Wallace (customer): Monday morning works. But David, if we're still seeing the same numbers Monday, I need escalation. I can't keep going back to my team with 'we're looking into it.'
[30] David Kim (aegis_staff): Completely fair. If the upgrade doesn't resolve it and we don't have a clear answer by Monday, I'll escalate this to our senior engineering team and loop in your account manager. You have my word on that.
[31] Kendra Wallace (customer): Alright. I'll hold you to that. Go ahead and send me those upgrade instructions and I'll get my team moving on it tonight.
[32] David Kim (aegis_staff): Will do. I'll have that in your inbox within the next thirty minutes. And Kendra — again, I'm sorry this dragged on as long as it did. We'll get it resolved.
[33] Kendra Wallace (customer): Appreciate it. Talk Monday.
[34] David Kim (aegis_staff): Talk Monday. Thanks Kendra, take care.
